title: Serving Runtime: Architecture, Scheduling, Profiling & Ops Playbook
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical serving-runtime playbook for Redwood Inference. It consolidates the runtime architecture, kernel scheduling policy, profiling and benchmarking playbooks, recent release notes, known issues, and operational runbooks used by the serving-runtime team. Use this as the first stop when diagnosing performance regressions, planning kernel/scheduler changes, or onboarding new runtime engineers.

Table of contents
- Architecture overview
- Kernel scheduling: objectives and policies
- Profiling playbook (how-to)
- Benchmarking suite: tests, metrics and CI
- Release notes (summary)
- Known issues and workarounds
- Runbooks: incident procedures
- Team wiki / ownership / contacts

1) Runtime architecture (high level)

Short summary
The serving runtime is composed of these primary components:
- Front door (API gateway / auth layer)
- Router (smart routing, variant selection, fallback)
- Scheduler (kernel selection, GPU allocation, preemption)
- Worker processes (per-GPU inference engines)
- KV-prefetch and prefix cache layer
- Quantization and kernel-bridge layer (FP16/int8 kernels)
- Telemetry/Tracing (open-telemetry + internal collectors)
- Observability and control plane (dashboards, rollouts, tracing hooks)

Design goals and constraints
- Predictable p95/p99 latency under mixed workloads
- High amortized throughput via batching and KV caching
- Graceful degradation: fallback to lower-cost kernels or model variants
- Deterministic behavior for rollout rollbacks and A/B tests

Service responsibilities and ownership
- Router + Scheduler: runtime-scheduling team (oncall: #runtime-oncall)
- Worker (inference engine): serving-runtime team (oncall: #serving-runtime-oncall)
- Observability + tracing: eng-platform (dashboards + logs)

2) Kernel scheduling: objectives and policies

Goals
- Minimize token latency for latency-sensitive tiers (PL/Enterprise latency tiers)
- Maximize throughput for batch workloads while respecting latency SLOs
- Avoid tail latency amplification when autoscaling or preempting

Key policies (priority order)
1. Latency tier isolation: requests tagged latency-sensitive are scheduled on low-concurrency nodes with warm KV caches.
2. Batch opportunistically: best-effort batching is allowed when it does not increase p95 beyond configured SLOs.
3. Fallback rules: if a kernel OOMs or exceeds 90% GPU mem for >30s, route to quantized or lower-width kernel.
4. Preemption policy: preempt batch jobs first; do not preempt running live inference streams except in emergency (manual override).

Scheduler parameters (common configuration)
- warm_worker_count: "2"  # number of warm workers to keep per model per zone
- max_concurrency_per_worker: "32"  # dependent on kernel and GPU memory profile
- batch_latency_target_ms: "25"  # target additional latency to allow for batching
- eviction_threshold_percent: "90"  # GPU mem pct to trigger fallback

Example scheduling decision (pseudocode)
- if request.tier == "latency-sensitive" and worker.kv_warm == true: route_to(worker_low_concurrency)
- else if worker.current_batch_latency < batch_latency_target_ms: attempt_batching()

3) Profiling playbook (how to run a diagnosis)

When to profile
- p95/p99 is above SLO for >10 minutes
- sudden increase in kernel OOMs or GPU memory fragmentation
- new release introduced kernel or scheduling changes

Step-by-step profiling flow
1) Collect telemetry
   - Export traces for the affected time window from tracing backend (example query):
     query: service="serving-runtime" AND model_id="{model}" AND timestamp:[start TO end]
2) Reproduce load (isolated staging)
   - Use benchmark harness (see section below) with the same prompt mix and batching config.
   - Command: 
     ./bench/run_bench.py --model redwood-xl-13b --concurrency 24 --prompt-set prompts/low-latency.json --duration 600
3) Capture GPU and kernel metrics during repro
   - nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1 > /tmp/gpu-dmon.csv
   - perf record -F 99 -g -- /opt/runtime/bin/inference_worker --model redwood-xl-13b
   - For CUDA kernels use nsight or CUPTI-based sampling: nvprof / ncu or nsys: nsys profile -o profile.nsys ./run_inference.sh
4) Generate artifacts
   - Flamegraphs: perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > perf.svg
   - pprof (Go runtime): pprof --http=:6060 /tmp/cpu.prof
   - Kernel-level timelines: nsys/ui or ncu report
5) Interpret common signatures
   - Long GC/CP heap stalls: indicates memory churn in worker -> check for large per-request allocations (string copies, serialization).
   - GPU mem fragmentation: repeated allocation failures followed by transient frees -> consider pre-alloc pool or increase warm_worker_count.
   - Kernel launch spikes: check kernel selection policy; fallback to a stable kernel if new kernels are failing.

Artifacts to attach to incident ticket
- Trace IDs, p95/p99 graphs, perf flamegraphs, nsys reports, GPU dmon snapshot, bench config used for repro.

4) Benchmarking suite: tests, metrics and CI integration

Suite summary
- Purpose: measure throughput, latency (p50/p95/p99), and unit cost for models across common hardware families and kernels.
- Test types: microbenchmarks (single-token), interactive benchmarks (chat-like workloads), and production-mix replay.

Key tests
- micro_latency: single-request, no batching, varying sequence length
- steady_throughput: constant QPS for 10m to measure thermal throttling and long-term stability
- burst_recovery: short high-QPS bursts to measure autoscale and cold-start cost
- production_replay: replay sampled production traffic (sanitized) to validate regression

Metrics and SLOs
- p50/p95/p99 (ms): reported for token generation and end-to-end request
- throughput (tokens/s) and tokens-per-dollar (cost metric)
- kernel_failure_rate: fraction of requests that triggered kernel fallback or OOM
- SLO example: latency-tier p95 < 120ms for 2k context on A100-80GB under 50% load; throughput baseline for model X on V100: 10k tokens/s

CI integration
- Benchmarks run nightly against release-candidate kernels. Any regression >5% on p95 triggers a blocking alert in the release pipeline.
- Commands to run locally: 
  - ./bench/setup_env.sh # creates conda env, installs deps
  - ./bench/run_suite.sh --hardware a100 --model redwood-xl-13b --suite production_replay --duration 600

Reporting
- Bench outputs are JSON in artifacts/ with keys: p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec, kernel_failure_rate. Example snippet: 
  {
    "model": "redwood-xl-13b",
    "hardware": "a100-80gb",
    "p95_ms": "98.2",
    "tokens_per_sec": "12400"
  }

5) Release notes (summary)

Release: serving-runtime v2026.02.28
Highlights
- New kernel: "int8-optimized-matmul-v2" enabled for redwood-xl-13b on A100. Expected improvement: 1.6x tokens/s, ~8% p95 latency reduction.
- Scheduler: added preemption policy that prefers batch preemption and added eviction_threshold_percent config.
- Observability: p99 breakdown per-kernel surface added to the dashboard.

Breaking changes / migration notes
- Default max_concurrency_per_worker reduced from 48 -> 32 for latency tiers. Customers pinned to older behavior should set per-model config max_concurrency_override.
- int8-optimized-matmul-v2 is enabled behind feature flag. To opt out set KERNEL_FLAGS="disable:v2-int8" in model config.

6) Known issues and workarounds

ISSUE-2026-001: intermittent kernel OOMs on a100-80gb during long-context (>4096) tokens\- Workaround: enable per-model pre-allocation (model_config.memory_pool="large") or reduce max_concurrency_per_worker to 16.
Owner: Diego Ramirez

ISSUE-2026-002: degraded p99 after rollout of int8-optimized-matmul-v2 on 13B model variants\- Workaround: rollback kernel flag and set rollout to canary=5% while collecting perf traces.
Owner: Marcus Li

ISSUE-2026-003: production-replay tool leaks file descriptors on long runs\- Workaround: restart bench controller every 2 hours; fix scheduled in next minor release.
Owner: Priya Singh

7) Runbooks: operational procedures (short, actionable)

Runbook A — High tail latency (p95/p99 above SLO)
1. Identify affected models/services via dashboards (select time window where anomaly started).
2. Check tracing for slow spans (router, scheduler, worker).
3. If worker spans are long: collect perf + nsys trace as per profiling playbook.
4. Temporarily reduce max_concurrency_per_worker for affected model to 16 to reduce queuing latency:
   - curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_TOKEN" "https://controlplane.internal/models/{model}/config" -d '{"max_concurrency_per_worker":16}'
5. If p99 drops, revert after investigation or raise rollout to stage incremental changes.

Runbook B — Kernel OOMs detected
1. Identify kernel and GPU type from logs: look for "OutOfMemoryError" and kernel name.
2. If widespread, enable fallback: set model kernel preference to fallback kernels.
   - Example API payload: {"kernel_preferences": ["quantized-int8", "fp16-stable"]}
3. If OOMs persist, set eviction_threshold_percent to 80% for the model to trigger earlier fallback.
4. Schedule a graceful rollout of a kernel patch with canary=2% and monitor kernel_failure_rate.

Runbook C — Degraded throughput (tokens/sec drop)
1. Check GPU utilization (dmon) and kernel launch rates.
2. If utilization is low but latency high, investigate stalls in CPU (data prep) and RPC latencies.
3. Increase warm_worker_count to reduce cold allocations for high-burst workloads.

8) Team wiki, ownership and contacts

Oncall and escalation
- Primary oncall: serving-runtime team (pagerduty: PD_ID_serving_runtime)
- Secondary: runtime-scheduling team
- Slack channels: #serving-runtime, #runtime-oncall, #infra-alerts

Docs and onboarding
- Quickstart: ./docs/onboarding/serving-runtime-quickstart.md
- Bench harness: ./bench/README.md
- Perf dashboards: https://grafana.internal/d/serving-runtime

Training and pairing
- New runtime engineers must run the bench suite, reproduce a regression, and present findings in the runtime weekly (owner: Asha Patel).

Appendix: useful commands and snippets
- Start a local worker with tracing enabled:
  OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=\"https://otel-collector.internal\" 
  ./bin/inference_worker --model redwood-xl-13b --port 5100 --log-level debug

- Short repro command for p95 regression:
  ./bench/run_bench.py --model redwood-xl-13b --concurrency 8 --prompt-set prompts/chat-1k.json --duration 300 --save-artifact /tmp/bench.json

- Example model config (YAML)
  model_id: redwood-xl-13b
  max_concurrency_per_worker: 32
  warm_worker_count: 2
  kernel_preferences: [\"fp16-stable\", \"quantized-int8\"]

References and related pages
- Serving runtime architecture (detailed): /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/serving-runtime-architecture-playbook-2026.json

If you are oncall and this document does not resolve the incident within 15 minutes, escalate to the secondary oncall and open an incident page (use the incident template: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process).
